comments.value: Are you able to verify and share what sample rate the microphone is running at? Can you tell if the microphone is dropping samples due to being in virtualization?

@{58c6cbcffd04b1785f747b6c|full_name}: I've used both 2ch, 16 bit and 32 bit, 48000hz. Also used the maximum sample rate; 2ch, 32 bit, 192000 Hz.
As for sample drop for virtualization, how would one check that??

@{61f11746876f6c7842f9c731|full_name}: I guess I would run VRC in a heavy world and record the mic in audacity or similar. To see if heavy load is causing weird issues. 
Even with this confirmed, I’m not sure what sort of odd behavior checks they do on voice, this is just a shot in the dark. I figure the more information you can provide the better.
I think a posting your client log would be in order too. Though, those are only so useful.

@{58c6cbcffd04b1785f747b6c|full_name}: I recorded on audacity while in Treehouse in the Shade with shaders on. The audio file came out fine and smooth. 
I don't know what files to put out, so I'm going to post the output log file when I crashed when I spoke in the audacity run and also the client log that is from four days ago, for I can't find another log for the client...

details:
Platform: Mac OSX with Parrallell Windows 11 playing VRChat in desktop mode
There seems to be an issue regarding my micophone information being sent to other players and causing an "Unusual Client Activity" 
My microphone works fine and is recognized in VRChat; when I am in a world alone and speak, I do not get kicked; but once there is another player and I speak or have the microphone pick up any sound, the game kicks me and states, "unusual client activity."
I've played VRChat on my oculus and it can play it fine with the same internet I have my computer connected to. 
I've used multiple microphones to see if that was the issue, Ive assigned my windows a personal microphone so it does not need to route it from the Mac OS. And still, i get kicked.
How can I fix this? 
Can this be fixed?
title: "Unusual Cleint Activity" when speaking with another player.
